b110.title: Consciousness functions
b110.description: General mental functions of the state of awareness and alertness, including the clarity and continuity of the wakeful state.

b1100.title: State of consciousness
b1100.description:
Mental functions that when altered produce states such as clouding of consciousness, stupor or coma.
Mental functions that produce consciousness, and when altered produce states such as clouding of consciousness, stupor or coma.

b1101.title: Continuity of consciousness
b1101.description: Mental functions that produce sustained wakefulness, alertness and awareness and, when disrupted, may produce fugue, trance or other similar states.

b1102.title: Quality of consciousness
b1102.description: Mental functions that when altered effect changes in the character of wakeful, alert and aware sentience, such as drug-induced altered states or delirium.

b114.title: Orientation functions
b114.description: General mental functions of knowing and ascertaining one's relation to time to place, to self, to others, to objects, and to space.

b1140.title: Orientation to time
b1140.description: Mental functions that produce awareness of time of the day, day of the week, date, month and year.

b1141.title: Orientation to place
b1141.description: Mental functions that produce awareness of one's location, such as one's immediate surroundings, one's town or country.

b1142.title: Orientation to person
b1142.description: Mental functions that produce awareness of one's own identity and of individuals in the immediate environment.

b11420.title: Orientation to self
b11420.description: Mental functions that produce awareness of one's own identity.

b11421.title: Orientation to others
b11421.description: Mental functions that produce awareness of the identity of other individuals in one's immediate environment.

b117.title: Intellectual functions
b117.description: General mental functions, required to understand and constructively integrate the various mental functions including all cognitive functions and their development over the life span.

b122.title: Global psychosocial functions
b122.description: General mental functions, as they develop over the life span, required to understand and constructively integrate the mental functions that lead to the formation of the personal skills needed to establish reciprocal social interactions, in terms of both meaning and purpose.

b126.title: Temperament and personality functions
b126.description: General mental functions of constitutional disposition of the individual to react in a particular way to situations, including the set of mental characteristics that makes the individual distinct from others.

b1260.title: Extraversion
b1260.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is outgoing, sociable and demonstrative, as contrasted to being shy, restricted and inhibited.

b1261.title: Agreeableness
b1261.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is cooperative, amicable, and accommodating, as contrasted to being unfriendly, oppositional and defiant.

b1262.title: Conscientiousness
b1262.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition such as in being hard-working, methodical and scrupulous, as contrasted to mental functions producing dispositions such as being lazy, unreliable and irresponsible.

b1263.title: Psychic stability
b1263.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is even-tempered, calm and composed, as contrasted to being irritable, worried, erratic and moody.

b1264.title: Openness to experience
b1264.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is curious, imaginative, inquisitive and experience-seeking, as contrasted to being stagnant, inattentive and emotionally inexpressive.

b1265.title: Optimism
b1265.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is cheerful, buoyant and hopeful, as contrasted to being downhearted, gloomy and despairing.

b1266.title: Confidence
b1266.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is self-assured, bold and assertive, as contrasted to being timid, insecure and self effacing.

b1267.title: Trustworthiness
b1267.description: Mental functions that produce a personal disposition that is dependable and principled, as contrasted to being deceitful and antisocial.

b130.title: Energy and drive functions
b130.description: General mental functions of physiological and psychological mechanisms that cause the individual to move towards satisfying specific needs and general goals in a persistent manner.

b1300.title: Energy level
b1300.description: Mental functions that produce vigour and stamina.

b1301.title: Motivation
b1301.description: Mental functions that produce the incentive to act; the conscious or unconscious driving force for action.

b1302.title: Appetite
b1302.description: Mental functions that produce a natural longing or desire, especially the natural and recurring desire for food and drink.

b1303.title: Craving
b1303.description: Mental functions that produce the urge to consume substances, including substances that can be abused.

b1304.title: Impulse control
b1304.description: Mental functions that regulate and resist sudden intense urges to do something.

b134.title: Sleep functions
b134.description: General mental functions of periodic, reversible and selective physical and mental disengagement from one's immediate environment accompanied by characteristic physiological changes.

b1340.title: Amount of sleep
b1340.description: Mental functions involved in the time spent in the state of sleep in the diurnal cycle or circadian rhythm.

b1341.title: Onset of sleep
b1341.description: Mental functions that produce the transition between wakefulness and sleep.

b1342.title: Maintenance of sleep
b1342.description: Mental functions that sustain the state of being asleep.

b1343.title: Quality of sleep
b1343.description: Mental functions that produce the natural sleep leading to optimal physical and mental rest and relaxation.

b1344.title: Functions involving the sleep cycle
b1344.description: Mental functions that produce rapid eye movement (REM) sleep (associated with dreaming) and non-rapid eye movement sleep (NREM) (characterized by the traditional concept of sleep as a time of decreased physiological and psychological activity).

b140.title: Attention functions
b140.description: Specific mental functions of focusing on an external stimulus or internal experience for the required period of time.

b1400.title: Sustaining attention
b1400.description: Mental functions that produce concentration for the period of time required.

b1401.title: Shifting attention
b1401.description: Mental functions that permit refocusing concentration from one stimulus to another.

b1402.title: Dividing attention
b1402.description: Mental functions that permit focusing on two or more stimuli at the same time.

b1403.title: Sharing attention
b1403.description: Mental functions that permit focusing on the same stimulus by two or more people, such as a child and a caregiver both focusing on a toy.

b144.title: Memory functions
b144.description: Specific mental functions of registering and storing information and retrieving it as needed.

b1440.title: Short-term memory
b1440.description: Mental functions that produce a temporary, disruptable memory store of around 30 seconds duration from which information is lost if not consolidated into long-term memory.

b1441.title: Long-term memory
b1441.description: Mental functions that produce a memory system permitting the long-term storage of information from short-term memory and both autobiographical memory for past events and semantic memory for language and facts.

b1442.title: Retrieval and processing of memory
b1442.description: Specific mental functions of recalling information stored in long-term memory and bringing it into awareness.

b147.title: Psychomotor functions
b147.description: Specific mental functions of control over both motor and psychological events at the body level.
exclusions: mental functions of sequencing complex movements

b1470.title: Psychomotor control
b1470.description: Mental functions that regulate the speed of behaviour or response time that involves both motor and psychological components, such as in disruption of control producing psychomotor retardation (moving and speaking slowly; decrease in gesturing and spontaneity) or psychomotor excitement (excessive behavioural and cognitive activity, usually nonproductive and often in response to inner tension as in toe-tapping, hand-wringing, agitation, or restlessness).

b1471.title: Quality of psychomotor functions
b1471.description: Mental functions that produce nonverbal behaviour in the proper sequence and character of its subcomponents, such as hand and eye coordination, or gait.

b152.title: Emotional functions
b152.description: Specific mental functions related to the feeling and affective components of the processes of the mind.

b1520.title: Appropriateness of emotion
b1520.description: Mental functions that produce congruence of feeling or affect with the situation, such as happiness at receiving good news.

b1521.title: Regulation of emotion
b1521.description: Mental functions that control the experience and display of affect.

b1522.title: Range of emotion
b1522.description: Mental functions that produce the spectrum of experience of arousal of affect or feelings such as love, hate, anxiousness, sorrow, joy, fear and anger.

b156.title: Perceptual functions
b156.description: Specific mental functions of recognizing and interpreting sensory stimuli.

b1560.title: Auditory perception
b1560.description: Mental functions involved in discriminating sounds, tones, pitches and other acoustic stimuli.

b1561.title: Visual perception
b1561.description: Mental functions involved in discriminating shape, size, colour and other ocular stimuli.

b1562.title: Olfactory perception
b1562.description: Mental functions involved in distinguishing differences in smells.

b1563.title: Gustatory perception
b1563.description: Mental functions involved in distinguishing differences in tastes, such as sweet, sour, salty and bitter stimuli, detected by the tongue.

b1564.title: Tactile perception
b1564.description: Mental functions involved in distinguishing differences in texture, such as rough or smooth stimuli, detected by touch.

b1565.title: Visuospatial perception
b1565.description: Mental function involved in distinguishing by sight the relative position of objects in the environment or in relation to oneself.

b160.title: Thought functions
b160.description: Specific mental functions related to the ideational component of the mind.

b1600.title: Pace of thought
b1600.description: Mental functions that govern speed of the thinking process.

b1601.title: Form of thought
b1601.description: Mental functions that organize the thinking process as to its coherence and logic.

b1602.title: Content of thought
b1602.description: Mental functions consisting of the ideas that are present in the thinking process and what is being conceptualized.

b1603.title: Control of thought
b1603.description: Mental functions that provide volitional control of thinking and are recognized as such by the person.

b164.title: Higher-level cognitive functions
b164.description: Specific mental functions especially dependent on the frontal lobes of the brain, including complex goal-directed behaviours such as decision-making, abstract thinking, planning and carrying out plans, mental flexibility, and deciding which behaviours are appropriate under what circumstances; often called executive functions.

b1640.title: Abstraction
b1640.description: Mental functions of creating general ideas, qualities or characteristics out of, and distinct from, concrete realities, specific objects or actual instances.

b1641.title: Organization and planning
b1641.description: Mental functions of coordinating parts into a whole, of systematizing; the mental function involved in developing a method of proceeding or acting.

b1642.title: Time management
b1642.description: Mental functions of ordering events in chronological sequence, allocating amounts of time to events and activities.

b1643.title: Cognitive flexibility
b1643.description: Mental functions of changing strategies, or shifting mental sets, especially as involved in problem-solving.

b1644.title: Insight
b1644.description: Mental functions of awareness and understanding of oneself and one's behaviour.

b1645.title: Judgement
b1645.description: Mental functions involved in discriminating between and evaluating different options, such as those involved in forming an opinion.

b1646.title: Problem Solving
b1646.description: Mental functions of identifying, analysing, and integrating incongruent or conflicting information into a solution.

b167.title: Mental functions of language
b167.description: Specific mental functions of recognizing and using signs, symbols and other components of a language.

b1670.title: Reception of language
b1670.description: Specific mental functions of decoding messages in spoken, written or other forms, such as sign language, to obtain their meaning.

b16700.title: Reception of spoken language
b16700.description: Mental functions of decoding spoken messages to obtain their meaning.

b16701.title: Reception of written language
b16701.description: Mental functions of decoding written messages to obtain their meaning.

b16702.title: Reception of sign language
b16702.description: Mental functions of decoding messages in languages that use signs made by hands and other movements, in order to obtain their meaning.

b1671.title: Expression of language
b1671.description: Specific mental functions necessary to produce meaningful messages in spoken, written, signed or other forms of language.

b16710.title: Expression of spoken language
b16710.description: Mental functions necessary to produce meaningful spoken messages.

b16711.title: Expression of written language
b16711.description: Mental functions necessary to produce meaningful written messages.

b16712.title: Expression of sign language
b16712.description: Mental functions to produce meaningful messages in languages that use signs made by hands and other movements.

b1672.title: Integrative language functions
b1672.description: Mental functions that organize semantic and symbolic meaning, grammatical structure and ideas for the production of messages in spoken, written or other forms of language.

b172.title: Calculation functions
b172.description: Specific mental functions of determination, approximation and manipulation of mathematical symbols and processes.

b1720.title: Simple calculation
b1720.description: Mental functions of computing with numbers, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

b1721.title: Complex calculation
b1721.description: Mental functions of translating word problems into arithmetic procedures, translating mathematical formulas into arithmetic procedures, and other complex manipulations involving numbers.

b176.title: Mental function of sequencing complex movements
b176.description: Specific mental functions of sequencing and co-ordinating complex, purposeful movements.
exclusions: Chapter 7 Neuromusculoskeletal and Movement Related Functions

b180.title: Experience of self and time functions
b180.description: Specific mental functions related to the awareness of one's identity, one's body, one's position in the reality of one's environment and of time.

b1800.title: Experience of self
b1800.description: Specific mental functions of being aware of one's own identity and one's position in the reality of one's environment around oneself.

b1801.title: Body image
b1801.description: Specific mental functions related to the representation and awareness of one's body.

b1802.title: Experience of time
b1802.description: Specific mental functions of the subjective experiences related to the length and passage of time.

b210.title: Seeing functions
b210.description: Sensory functions relating to sensing the presence of light and sensing the form, size, shape and colour of the visual stimuli.

b2100.title: Visual acuity functions
b2100.description: Seeing functions of sensing form and contour, both binocular and monocular, for both distant and near vision.

b21000.title: Binocular acuity of distant vision
b21000.description: Seeing functions of sensing size, form and contour using both eyes for objects distant from the eye.

b21001.title: Monocular acuity of distant vision
b21001.description: Seeing functions of sensing size, form and contour using either right or left eye alone, for objects distant from the eye.

b21002.title: Binocular acuity of near vision
b21002.description: Seeing functions of sensing size, form and contour, using both eyes, for objects close to the eye.

b21003.title: Monocular acuity of near vision
b21003.description: Seeing functions of sensing size, form and contour, using either right or left eye alone, for objects close to the eye.

b2101.title: Visual field functions
b2101.description: Seeing functions related to the entire area that can be seen with fixation of gaze.

b2102.title: Quality of vision
b2102.description: Seeing functions involving light sensitivity, colour vision, contrast sensitivity and the overall quality of the picture.

b21020.title: Light sensitivity
b21020.description: Seeing functions of sensing a minimum amount of light (light minimum), and the minimum difference in intensity (light difference).

b21021.title: Colour vision
b21021.description: Seeing functions of differentiating and matching colours.

b21022.title: Contrast sensitivity
b21022.description: Seeing functions of separating figure from ground, involving the minimum amount of luminance required.

b21023.title: Visual picture quality
b21023.description: Seeing functions involving the quality of the picture.

b215.title: Functions of structures adjoining the eye
b215.description: Functions of structures in and around the eye that facilitate seeing functions.

b2150.title: Functions of internal muscles of the eye
b2150.description: Functions of the muscles inside the eye, such as the iris, that adjust the shape and size of the pupil and lens of the eye.

b2151.title: Functions of the eyelid
b2151.description: Functions of the eyelid, such as the protective reflex.

b2152.title: Functions of external muscles of the eye
b2152.description: Functions of the muscles that are used to look in different directions, to follow an object as it moves across the visual field, to produce saccadic jumps to catch up with a moving target, and to fix the eye.

b2153.title: Functions of lachrymal glands
b2153.description: Functions of the tear glands and ducts.

b220.title: Sensations associated with the eye and adjoining structures
b220.description: Sensations of tired, dry and itching eye and related feelings.
inclusions: feelings of pressure behind the eye

b230.title: Hearing functions
b230.description: Sensory functions relating to sensing the presence of sounds and discriminating the location, pitch, loudness and quality of sounds.

b2300.title: Sound detection
b2300.description: Sensory functions relating to sensing the presence of sounds.

b2301.title: Sound discrimination
b2301.description: Sensory functions relating to sensing the presence of sound involving the differentiation of ground and binaural synthesis, separation and blending.

b2302.title: Localization of sound source
b2302.description: Sensory functions relating to determining the location of the source of sound.

b2303.title: Lateralization of sound
b2303.description: Sensory functions relating to determining whether the sound is coming from right or the left side.

b2304.title: Speech discrimination
b2304.description: Sensory functions relating to determining spoken language and distinguishing it from other sounds.

b235.title: Vestibular functions
b235.description: Sensory functions of the inner ear related to position, balance and movement.
exclusions: sensation associated with hearing and vestibular functions

b2350.title: Vestibular function of position
b2350.description: Sensory functions of the inner ear related to determining the position of the body.

b2351.title: Vestibular function of balance
b2351.description: Sensory functions of the inner ear related to determining the balance of the body.

b2352.title: Vestibular function of determination of movement
b2352.description: Sensory functions of the inner ear related to determining movement of the body, including its direction and speed.

b240.title: Sensations associated with hearing and vestibular functions
b240.description: Sensations of dizziness, falling, tinnitus and vertigo.

b2400.title: Ringing in ears or tinnitus
b2400.description: Sensation of low-pitched rushing, hissing or ringing in the ear.

b2401.title: Dizziness
b2401.description: Sensation of motion involving either oneself or one's environment; sensation of rotating, swaying or tilting.

b2402.title: Sensation of falling
b2402.description: Sensation of losing one's grip and falling.

b2403.title: Nausea associated with dizziness or vertigo
b2403.description: Sensation of wanting to vomit that arises from dizziness or vertigo.

b2404.title: Irritation in the ear
b2404.description: Sensation of itching or other similar sensations in the ear.

b2405.title: Aural pressure
b2405.description: Sensation of pressure in the ear.

b250.title: Taste function
b250.description: Sensory functions of sensing qualities of bitterness, sweetness, sourness and saltiness.

b255.title: Smell function
b255.description: Sensory functions of sensing odours and smells.

b260.title: Proprioceptive function
b260.description: Sensory functions of sensing the relative position of body parts.
exclusions: Sensations related to muscles and movement functions

b265.title: Touch function
b265.description: Sensory functions of sensing surfaces and their texture or quality.
exclusions: Sensory functions related to temperature and other stimuli

b270.title: Sensory functions related to temperature and other stimuli
b270.description: Sensory functions of sensing temperature, vibration, pressure and noxious stimulus.

b2700.title: Sensitivity to temperature
b2700.description: Sensory functions of sensing cold and heat.

b2701.title: Sensitivity to vibration
b2701.description: Sensory functions of sensing shaking or oscillation.

b2702.title: Sensitivity to pressure
b2702.description: Sensory functions of sensing pressure against or on the skin.

b2703.title: Sensitivity to a noxious stimulus
b2703.description: Sensory functions of sensing painful or uncomfortable sensations.

b280.title: Sensation of pain
b280.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure.
inclusions: sensations of generalized or localized pain

b2800.title: Generalized pain
b2800.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt all over, or throughout the body.

b2801.title: Pain in body part
b2801.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in a specific part, or parts, of the body.

b28010.title: Pain in head and neck
b28010.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in the head and neck.

b28011.title: Pain in chest
b28011.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in the chest.

b28012.title: Pain in stomach or abdomen
b28012.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in the stomach or abdomen.

b28013.title: Pain in back
b28013.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in the back.

b28014.title: Pain in upper limb
b28014.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in either one or both upper limbs, including hands.

b28015.title: Pain in lower limb
b28015.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in either one or both lower limbs, including feet.

b28016.title: Pain in joints
b28016.description: Sensation of unpleasant feeling indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure felt in one or more joints, including small and big joints.

b2802.title: Pain in multiple body parts
b2802.description: Unpleasant sensation indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure located in several body parts.

b2803.title: Radiating pain in a dermatome
b2803.description: Unpleasant sensation indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure located in areas of skin served by the same nerve root.

b2804.title: Radiating pain in a segment or region
b2804.description: Unpleasant sensation indicating potential or actual damage to some body structure located in areas of skin in different body parts not served by the same nerve root.

b310.title: Voice functions
b310.description: Functions of the production of various sounds by the passage of air through the larynx.

b3100.title: Production of voice
b3100.description: Functions of the production of sound made through coordination of the larynx and surrounding muscles with the respiratory system.

b3101.title: Quality of voice
b3101.description: Functions of the production of characteristics of voice including pitch, resonance and other features.
inclusions: functions of high or low pitch

b320.title: Articulation functions
b320.description: Functions of the production of speech sounds.

b330.title: Fluency and rhythm of speech functions
b330.description: Functions of the production of flow and tempo of speech.

b3300.title: Fluency of speech
b3300.description: Functions of the production of smooth, uninterrupted flow of speech.
inclusions: functions of smooth connection of speech

b3301.title: Rhythm of speech
b3301.description: Functions of the modulated, tempo and stress patterns in speech.

b3302.title: Speed of speech
b3302.description: Functions of the rate of speech production.

b3303.title: Melody of speech
b3303.description: Functions of modulation of pitch patterns in speech.

b340.title: Alternative vocalization functions
b340.description: Functions of the production of other manners of vocalization.
exclusions: Fluency and rhythm of speech functions

b3400.title: Production of tones
b3400.description: Functions of production of musical vocal sounds.
inclusions: sustaining, modulating and terminating production of single or connected vocalizations with variation in pitch such as in singing, humming and chanting

b3401.title: Making a range of sounds
b3401.description: Functions of production of a variety of vocalizations.

b410.title: Heart functions
b410.description: Functions of pumping the blood in adequate or required amounts and pressure throughout the body.
inclusions: dynamics of circulation to the heart

b4100.title: Heart rate
b4100.description: Functions related to the number of times the heart contracts every minute.

b4101.title: Heart rhythm
b4101.description: Functions related to the regularity of the beating of the heart.

b4102.title: Contraction force of ventricular muscles
b4102.description: Functions related to the amount of blood pumped by the ventricular muscles during every beat.

b4103.title: Blood supply to the heart
b4103.description: Functions related to the volume of blood available to the heart muscle.

b415.title: Blood vessel functions
b415.description: Functions of transporting blood throughout the body.

b4150.title: Functions of arteries
b4150.description: Functions related to blood flow in the arteries.

b4151.title: Functions of capillaries
b4151.description: Functions related to blood flow in the capillaries.

b4152.title: Functions of veins
b4152.description: Functions related to blood flow in the veins, and the functions of valves of veins.

b420.title: Blood pressure functions
b420.description: Functions of maintaining the pressure of blood within the arteries.

b4200.title: Increased blood pressure
b4200.description: Functions related to a rise in systolic or diastolic blood pressure above normal for the age.

b4201.title: Decreased blood pressure
b4201.description: Functions related to a fall in systolic or diastolic blood pressure below normal for the age.

b4202.title: Maintenance of blood pressure
b4202.description: Functions related to maintaining an appropriate blood pressure in response to changes in the body.

b430.title: Haematological system functions
b430.description: Functions of blood production, oxygen and metabolite carriage, and clotting.
inclusions: functions of the production of bone marrow

b4300.title: Production of blood
b4300.description: Functions related to the production of blood and all its constituents.

b4301.title: Oxygen-carrying functions of the blood
b4301.description: Functions related to the blood's capacity to carry oxygen throughout the body.

b4302.title: Metabolite-carrying functions of the blood
b4302.description: Functions related to the blood's capacity to carry metabolites throughout the body.

b4303.title: Clotting functions
b4303.description: Functions related to the coagulation of blood, such as at a site of injury.

b435.title: Immunological system functions
b435.description: Functions of the body related to protection against foreign substances, including infections, by specific and non-specific immune responses.

b4350.title: Immune response
b4350.description: Functions of the body's response of sensitization to foreign substances, including infections.

b43500.title: Specific immune response
b43500.description: Functions of the body's response of sensitization to a specific foreign substance.

b43501.title: Non-specific immune response
b43501.description: Functions of the body's general response of sensitization to foreign substances, including infections.

b4351.title: Hypersensitivity reactions
b4351.description: Functions of the body's response of increased sensitization to foreign substances, such as in sensitivities to different antigens.

b4352.title: Functions of lymphatic vessels
b4352.description: Functions related to vascular channels that transport lymph.

b4353.title: Functions of lymph nodes
b4353.description: Functions related to glands along the course of lymphatic vessels.

b440.title: Respiration functions
b440.description: Functions of inhaling air into the lungs, the exchange of gases between air and blood, and exhaling air.

b4400.title: Respiration rate
b4400.description: Functions related to the number of breaths taken per minute.

b4401.title: Respiratory rhythm
b4401.description: Functions related to the periodicity and regularity of breathing.

b4402.title: Depth of respiration
b4402.description: Functions related to the volume of expansion of the lungs during breathing.

b445.title: Respiratory muscle functions
b445.description: Functions of the muscles involved in breathing.

b4450.title: Functions of the thoracic respiratory muscles
b4450.description: Functions of the thoracic muscles involved in breathing.

b4451.title: Functions of the diaphragm
b4451.description: Functions of the diaphragm as involved in breathing.

b4452.title: Functions of accessory respiratory muscles
b4452.description: Functions of the additional muscles involved in breathing.

b450.title: Additional functions of the respiratory system
b450.description: Additional functions related to breathing, such as producing and transporting secretion, coughing, sneezing and yawning.

b455.title: Exercise tolerance functions
b455.description: Functions related to respiratory and cardiovascular capacity as required for enduring physical exertion.

b4550.title: General physical endurance
b4550.description: Functions related to the general level of tolerance of physical exercise or stamina.

b4551.title: Aerobic capacity
b4551.description: Functions related to the extent to which a person can exercise without getting out of breath.
inclusions: extent of exercise without getting out of breath

b4552.title: Fatiguability
b4552.description: Functions related to susceptibility to fatigue, at any level of exertion.

b460.title: Sensations associated with cardiovascular and respiratory functions
b460.description: Sensations such as missing a heart beat, palpitation and shortness of breath.

b510.title: Ingestion functions
b510.description: Functions related to taking in and manipulating solids or liquids through the mouth into the body.

b5100.title: Sucking
b5100.description: Functions of drawing food or liquids into the mouth by a suction force produced by movements of the cheeks, lips and tongue.

b5101.title: Biting
b5101.description: Functions of cutting into, piercing or tearing off food with the front teeth.

b5102.title: Chewing
b5102.description: Functions of crushing, grinding and masticating food with the back teeth (e.g. molars).

b5103.title: Manipulation of food in the mouth
b5103.description: Functions of moving food around the mouth with the teeth and tongue.

b5104.title: Salivation
b5104.description: Function of the production of saliva within the mouth.

b5105.title: Swallowing
b5105.description: Functions of clearing substances, such as food, drink and saliva through the oral cavity, pharynx and oesophagus into the stomach at an appropriate rate and speed.

b51050.title: Oral swallowing
b51050.description: Function of clearing substances through the oral cavity at an appropriate rate and speed.

b51051.title: Pharyngeal swallowing
b51051.description: Function of clearing substances through the pharynx at an appropriate rate and speed.

b51052.title: Oesophageal swallowing
b51052.description: Function of clearing substances through the oesophagus at an appropriate rate and speed.

b5106.title: Functions of expelling the contents of the stomach, oesophagus or pharynx
b5106.description: Functions of moving substances such as food, liquid, medications, objects intentionally or unintentionally swallowed in the reverse direction to ingestion, such as in regurgitation and vomiting.

b515.title: Digestive functions
b515.description: Functions of transporting food through the gastrointestinal tract, breakdown of food and absorption of nutrients.
exclusions: Sensations associated with the digestive system

b5150.title: Transport of food through stomach and intestines
b5150.description: Peristalsis and related functions that mechanically move food through stomach and intestines.
inclusions: enzyme production and action in stomach and intestines

b5151.title: Breakdown of food
b5151.description: Functions of mechanically reducing food to smaller particles in the gastrointestinal tract.

b5152.title: Absorption of nutrients
b5152.description: Functions of passing food and drink nutrients into the blood stream from along the intestines.

b5153.title: Tolerance to food
b5153.description: Functions of accepting suitable food and drink for digestion and rejecting what is unsuitable.

b520.title: Assimilation functions
b520.description: Functions by which nutrients are converted into components of the living body.
inclusions: functions of storage of nutrients in the body

b525.title: Defecation functions
b525.description: Functions of elimination of wastes and undigested food as faeces and related functions.
exclusions: Sensations associated with the digestive system

b5250.title: Elimination of faeces
b5250.description: Functions of the elimination of waste from the rectum, including the functions of contraction of the abdominal muscles in doing so.

b5251.title: Faecal consistency
b5251.description: Consistency of faeces such as hard, firm, soft or watery.

b5252.title: Frequency of defecation
b5252.description: Functions involved in the frequency of defecation.

b5253.title: Faecal continence
b5253.description: Functions involved in voluntary control over the elimination function.

b5254.title: Flatulence
b5254.description: Functions involved in the expulsion of excessive amounts of air or gases from the intestines.

b530.title: Weight maintenance functions
b530.description: Functions of maintaining appropriate body weight, including weight gain during the developmental period.
inclusions: maintenance of acceptable Body Mass Index (BMI)

b535.title: Sensations associated with the digestive system
b535.description: Sensations arising from eating, drinking and related digestive functions.

b5351.title: Feeling bloated
b5351.description: Sensation of distension of the stomach or abdomen.

b5352.title: Sensation of abdominal cramp
b5352.description: Sensation of spasmodic or painful muscular contractions of the smooth muscles of the gastrointestinal tract.

b540.title: General metabolic functions
b540.description: Functions of regulation of essential components of the body such as carbohydrates, proteins and fats, the conversion of one to another, and their breakdown into energy.
exclusions: Water, mineral and electrolyte balance functions

b5400.title: Basal metabolic rate
b5400.description: Functions involved in oxygen consumption of the body at specified conditions of rest and temperature.

b5401.title: Carbohydrate metabolism
b5401.description: Functions involved in the process by which carbohydrates in the diet are stored and broken down into glucose and subsequently into carbon dioxide and water.

b5402.title: Protein metabolism
b5402.description: Functions involved in the process by which proteins in the diet are converted to amino acids and broken down further in the body.

b5403.title: Fat metabolism
b5403.description: Functions involved in the process by which fat in the diet is stored and broken down in the body.

b545.title: Water, mineral and electrolyte balance functions
b545.description: Functions of the regulation of water, minerals and electrolytes in the body.

b5450.title: Water balance
b5450.description: Functions involved in maintaining the level or amount of water in the body.

b54500.title: Water retention
b54500.description: Functions involved in keeping water in the body.

b54501.title: Maintenance of water balance
b54501.description: Functions involved in maintaining the optimal amount of water in the body.

b5451.title: Mineral balance
b5451.description: Functions involved in maintaining an equilibrium between intake, storage, utilization and excretion of minerals in the body.
inclusions: balance of minerals such as calcium

b5452.title: Electrolyte balance
b5452.description: Functions involved in maintaining an equilibrium between intake, storage, utilization and excretion of electrolytes in the body.

b550.title: Thermoregulatory functions
b550.description: Functions of the regulation of body temperature.

b5500.title: Body temperature
b5500.description: Functions involved in regulating the core temperature of the body.

b5501.title: Maintenance of body temperature
b5501.description: Functions involved in maintaining optimal body temperature as environmental temperature changes.

b555.title: Endocrine gland functions
b555.description: Functions of production and regulation of hormonal levels in the body, including cyclical changes.
exclusions: Water, mineral and electrolyte balance functions

b610.title: Urinary excretory functions
b610.description: Functions of filtration and collection of the urine.

b6100.title: Filtration of urine
b6100.description: Functions of filtration of urine by the kidneys.

b6101.title: Collection of urine
b6101.description: Functions of collection and storage of urine by the ureters and bladder.

b620.title: Urination functions
b620.description: Functions of discharge of urine from the urinary bladder.

b6200.title: Urination
b6200.description: Functions of voiding the urinary bladder.

b6201.title: Frequency of urination
b6201.description: Functions involved in the number of times urination occurs.

b630.title: Sensations associated with urinary functions
b630.description: Sensations arising from voiding and related urinary functions.
inclusions: sensations of incomplete voiding of urine

b640.title: Sexual functions
b640.description: Mental and physical functions related to the sexual act, including the arousal, preparatory, orgasmic and resolution stages.
exclusions: Sensations associated with genital and reproductive functions

b6400.title: Functions of sexual arousal phase
b6400.description: Functions of sexual interest and excitement.

b6401.title: Functions of sexual preparatory phase
b6401.description: Functions of engaging in sexual intercourse.

b6403.title: Functions of sexual resolution phase
b6403.description: Functions of satisfaction after orgasm and accompanying relaxation.

b650.title: Menstruation functions
b650.description: Functions associated with the menstrual cycle, including regularity of menstruation and discharge of menstrual fluids.
exclusions: Sensations associated with genital and reproductive functions

b6500.title: Regularity of menstrual cycle
b6500.description: Functions involved in the regularity of the menstrual cycle.

b6501.title: Interval between menstruation
b6501.description: Functions relating to the length of time between two menstrual cycles.

b6502.title: Extent of menstrual bleeding
b6502.description: Functions involved in the quantity of menstrual flow.

b660.title: Procreation functions
b660.description: Functions associated with fertility, pregnancy, childbirth and lactation.

b6600.title: Functions related to fertility
b6600.description: Functions related to the ability to produce gametes for procreation.

b6601.title: Functions related to pregnancy
b6601.description: Functions involved in becoming pregnant and being pregnant.

b6603.title: Lactation
b6603.description: Functions involved in the production of milk and making it available to the child.

b670.title: Sensations associated with genital and reproductive functions
b670.description: Sensations associated with sexual intercourse, menstruation, and related genital or reproductive functions.

b6700.title: Sensations associated with sexual intercourse
b6700.description: Sensations associated with sexual arousal, preparation, intercourse, orgasm and resolution.

b6701.title: Sensations associated with the menstrual cycle
b6701.description: Sensations involved with menstruation, including pre- and post-menstrual phases.

b6702.title: Sensations associated with menopause
b6702.description: Sensations associated with the cessation of menstrual cycle.

b710.title: Mobility of joint functions
b710.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of a joint.

b7100.title: Mobility of a single joint
b7100.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of one joint.

b7101.title: Mobility of several joints
b7101.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of more than one joint.
inclusions: mobility of small joints of feet
mobility of small joints of hands

b7102.title: Mobility of joints generalized
b7102.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of joints throughout the body.

b715.title: Stability of joint functions
b715.description: Functions of the maintenance of structural integrity of the joints.

b7150.title: Stability of a single joint
b7150.description: Functions of the maintenance of structural integrity of one joint.

b7151.title: Stability of several joints
b7151.description: Functions of the maintenance of structural integrity of more than one joint.

b7152.title: Stability of joints generalized
b7152.description: Functions of the maintenance of structural integrity of joints throughout the body.

b720.title: Mobility of bone functions
b720.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of the scapula, pelvis, carpal and tarsal bones.

b7200.title: Mobility of scapula
b7200.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of the scapula.

b7201.title: Mobility of pelvis
b7201.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of the pelvis.

b7202.title: Mobility of carpal bones
b7202.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of the carpal bones.

b7203.title: Mobility of tarsal bones
b7203.description: Functions of the range and ease of movement of the tarsal bones.

b730.title: Muscle power functions
b730.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of a muscle or muscle groups.
exclusions: Functions of structures adjoining the eye

b7300.title: Power of isolated muscles and muscle groups
b7300.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of specific and isolated muscles and muscle groups.

b7301.title: Power of muscles of one limb
b7301.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of the muscles and muscle groups of one arm or leg.

b7302.title: Power of muscles of one side of the body
b7302.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of the muscles and muscle groups found on the left or right side of the body.

b7303.title: Power of muscles in lower half of the body
b7303.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of the muscles and muscle groups found in the lower half of the body.

b7304.title: Power of muscles of all limbs
b7304.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of muscles and muscle groups of all four limbs.

b7305.title: Power of muscles of the trunk
b7305.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of muscles and muscle groups in the trunk.

b7306.title: Power of all muscles of the body
b7306.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of all muscles and muscle groups of the body.

b735.title: Muscle tone functions
b735.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and the resistance offered when trying to move the muscles passively.

b7350.title: Tone of isolated muscles and muscle groups
b7350.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting isolated muscles and muscle groups and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b7351.title: Tone of muscles of one limb
b7351.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and muscle groups in one arm or leg and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b7352.title: Tone of muscles of one side of body
b7352.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and muscle groups of the right or left side of the body and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b7353.title: Tone of muscles of lower half of body
b7353.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and muscle groups in the lower half of the body and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b7354.title: Tone of muscles of all limbs
b7354.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and muscle groups in all four limbs and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b7355.title: Tone of muscles of trunk
b7355.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and muscle groups of the trunk and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b7356.title: Tone of all muscles of the body
b7356.description: Functions related to the tension present in the resting muscles and muscle groups of the whole body and the resistance offered when trying to move those muscles passively.

b740.title: Muscle endurance functions
b740.description: Functions related to sustaining muscle contraction for the required period of time.

b7400.title: Endurance of isolated muscles
b7400.description: Functions related to sustaining muscle contraction of isolated muscles for the required period of time.

b7401.title: Endurance of muscle groups
b7401.description: Functions related to sustaining muscle contraction of isolated muscle groups for the required period of time.

b7402.title: Endurance of all muscles of the body
b7402.description: Functions related to sustaining muscle contraction of all muscles of the body for the required period of time.

b750.title: Motor reflex functions
b750.description: Functions of involuntary contraction of muscles automatically induced by specific stimuli.

b7500.title: Stretch motor reflex
b7500.description: Functions of involuntary contractions of muscles automatically induced by stretching.

b7501.title: Reflexes generated by noxious stimuli
b7501.description: Functions of involuntary contractions of muscles automatically induced by painful or other noxious stimuli.

b7502.title: Reflexes generated by other exteroceptive stimuli
b7502.description: Functions of involuntary contractions of muscles automatically induced by external stimuli other than noxious stimuli.

b755.title: Involuntary movement reaction functions
b755.description: Functions of involuntary contractions of large muscles or the whole body induced by body position, balance and threatening stimuli.

b760.title: Control of voluntary movement functions
b760.description: Functions associated with control over and coordination of voluntary movements.

b7600.title: Control of simple voluntary movements
b7600.description: Functions associated with control over and coordination of simple or isolated voluntary movements.

b7601.title: Control of complex voluntary movements
b7601.description: Functions associated with control over and coordination of complex voluntary movements.

b7602.title: Coordination of voluntary movements
b7602.description: Functions associated with coordination of simple and complex voluntary movements, performing movements in an orderly combination.

b7603.title: Supportive functions of arm or leg
b7603.description: Functions associated with control over and coordination of voluntary movements by placing weight either on the arms (elbows or hands) or on the legs (knees or feet).

b765.title: Involuntary movement functions
b765.description: Functions of unintentional, non- or semi-purposive involuntary contractions of a muscle or group of muscles.

b7650.title: Involuntary contractions of muscles
b7650.description: Functions of unintentional, non- or semi-purposive involuntary contractions of a muscle or group of muscles, such as those involved in part of a psychological dysfunction.

b7651.title: Tremor
b7651.description: Functions of alternating contraction and relaxation of a group of muscles around a joint, resulting in shakiness.

b7652.title: Tics and mannerisms
b7652.description: Functions of repetitive, quasi-purposive, involuntary contractions of a group of muscles.

b7653.title: Stereotypies and motor perseveration
b7653.description: Functions of spontaneous, non-purposive movements such as repetitively rocking to and fro and nodding the head or wiggling.

b770.title: Gait pattern functions
b770.description: Functions of movement patterns associated with walking, running or other whole body movements.

b780.title: Sensations related to muscles and movement functions
b780.description: Sensations associated with the muscles or muscle groups of the body and their movement.

b7800.title: Sensation of muscle stiffness
b7800.description: Sensation of tightness or stiffness of muscles.

b7801.title: Sensation of muscle spasm
b7801.description: Sensation of involuntary contraction of a muscle or a group of muscles.

b810.title: Protective functions of the skin
b810.description: Functions of the skin for protecting the body from physical, chemical and biological threats.
inclusions: functions of protecting against the sun and other radiation

b820.title: Repair functions of the skin
b820.description: Functions of the skin for repairing breaks and other damage to the skin.

b830.title: Other functions of the skin
b830.description: Functions of the skin other than protection and repair, such as regulating body temperature via sweat, regulating changes in peripheral circulation and fluid balance via sweat, reservoir for the synthesis of vitamin D.
inclusions: glandular functions of the skin and resulting body odour

b840.title: Sensation related to the skin
b840.description: Sensations related to the skin such as itching, burning sensation and tingling.

b850.title: Functions of hair
b850.description: Functions of the hair, such as protection, coloration and appearance.

b860.title: Functions of nails
b860.description: Functions of the nails, such as protection, scratching and appearance.

d110.title: Watching
d110.description: Using the sense of seeing intentionally to experience visual stimuli, such as visually tracking an object, watching a sporting event, people, or children playing.

d115.title: Listening
d115.description: Using the sense of hearing intentionally to experience auditory stimuli, such as listening to a radio, to the human voice, to music, to a lecture, or to a story told.

d120.title: Other purposeful sensing
d120.description: Using the body's other basic senses intentionally to experience stimuli, such as touching and feeling textures, tasting sweets or smelling flowers.

d130.title: Copying
d130.description: Imitating or mimicking as a basic component of learning, such as copying a facial expression, a gesture, a sound or the letters of an alphabet.

d135.title: Rehearsing
d135.description: Repeating a sequence of events or symbols as a basic component of learning, such as counting by tens or practising the recitation of a rhyme with gestures or cords on a musical instrument.

d140.title: Learning to read
d140.description: Developing the competence to read written material (including Braille and other symbols) with fluency and accuracy, such as recognizing characters and alphabet letters, sounding out written words with correct pronunciation, and understanding written words and phrases.

d145.title: Learning to write
d145.description: Developing the competence to produce symbols that represent sounds, words or phrases in order to convey meaning (including Braille writing, and other symbols), such as spelling and effectively using correct grammar.

d150.title: Learning to calculate
d150.description: Developing the competence to manipulate numbers and perform simple and complex mathematical operations, such as using mathematical signs for addition and subtraction and applying the correct mathematical operation to a problem.

d155.title: Acquiring skills
d155.description: Developing basic and complex competencies in integrated sets of actions or tasks so as to initiate and follow through with the acquisition of a skill, such as manipulating tools or toys or playing games.

d1550.title: Acquiring basic skills
d1550.description: Learning elementary, purposeful actions, such as learning to use simple tools, such as pencils or eating utensils.

d1551.title: Acquiring complex skills
d1551.description: Learning integrated sets of actions so as to follow rules, and to sequence and coordinate one's movements, such as learning to play games (e.g. football or chess) and to use a building tool.

d160.title: Focusing attention
d160.description: Intentionally focusing on specific stimuli, such as by filtering out distracting noises.

d163.title: Thinking
d163.description: Formulating and manipulating ideas, concepts, and images, whether goal-oriented or not, either alone or with others, such as creating fiction, proving a theorem, playing with ideas, brainstorming, meditating, pondering, speculating, or reflecting.

d166.title: Reading
d166.description: Performing activities involved in the comprehension and interpretation of written language (e.g. books, instructions or newspapers in text or Braille), for the purpose of obtaining general knowledge or specific information.

d170.title: Writing
d170.description: Using or producing symbols or language to convey information, such as producing a written record of events or ideas or drafting a letter.

d172.title: Calculating
d172.description: Performing computations by applying mathematical principles to solve problems that are described in words and producing or displaying the results, such as computing the sum of three numbers or finding the result of dividing one number by another.

d175.title: Solving problems
d175.description: Finding solutions to questions or situations by identifying and analysing issues, developing options and solutions, evaluating potential effects of solutions, and executing a chosen solution, such as in resolving a dispute between two people.

d1750.title: Solving simple problems
d1750.description: Finding solutions to a simple problem involving a single issue or question, by identifying and analysing the issue, developing solutions, evaluating the potential effects of the solutions and executing a chosen solution.

d1751.title: Solving complex problems
d1751.description: Finding solutions to a complex problem involving multiple and interrelated issues, or several related problems, by identifying and analysing the issue, developing solutions, evaluating the potential effects of the solutions and executing a chosen solution.

d177.title: Making decisions
d177.description: Making a choice among options, implementing the choice, and evaluating the effects of the choice, such as selecting and purchasing a specific item, or deciding to undertake and undertaking one task from among several tasks that need to be done.

d210.title: Undertaking a single task
d210.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions related to the mental and physical components of a single task, such as initiating a task, organizing time, space and materials for a task, pacing task performance, and carrying out, completing, and sustaining a task.

d2100.title: Undertaking a simple task
d2100.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space required for a simple task; executing a simple task with a single major component, such as packing objects into a container.

d2101.title: Undertaking a complex task
d2101.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space for a complex task; executing a complex task with more than one component, which may be carried out in sequence or simultaneously, such as making up a place for playing, arranging the furniture in one's home or completing an assignment for school.

d2102.title: Undertaking a single task independently
d2102.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space for a simple or complex task; managing and executing a task on one's own and without the assistance of others.

d2103.title: Undertaking a single task in a group
d2103.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space for a single task, simple or complex; managing and executing a task with people who are involved in some or all steps of the task.

d220.title: Undertaking multiple tasks
d220.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions as components of multiple, integrated and complex tasks in sequence or simultaneously.

d2200.title: Carrying out multiple tasks
d2200.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space needed for several tasks, and managing and executing several tasks, together or sequentially.

d2201.title: Completing multiple tasks
d2201.description: Completing several tasks, together or sequentially.

d2202.title: Undertaking multiple tasks independently
d2202.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space for multiple tasks, and managing and executing several tasks together or sequentially, on one's own and without the assistance of others.

d2203.title: Undertaking multiple tasks in a group
d2203.description: Preparing, initiating and arranging the time and space for multiple tasks, and managing and executing several tasks together or sequentially with others who are involved in some or all steps of the multiple tasks.

d230.title: Carrying out daily routine
d230.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions in order to plan, manage and complete the requirements of day-to-day procedures or duties, such as budgeting time and making plans for separate activities throughout the day.

d2301.title: Managing daily routine
d2301.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions in order to plan and manage the requirements of day-to-day procedures or duties.

d2302.title: Completing the daily routine
d2302.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions in order to complete the requirements of usual day-to-day procedures or duties, such as getting dressed, eating breakfast, leaving for school or work and returning home at the end of the day.

d2303.title: Managing one's own activity level
d2303.description: Carrying out actions and behaviours to arrange the requirements in energy and time day-to-day procedures or duties.

d240.title: Handling stress and other psychological demands
d240.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions to manage and control the psychological demands required to carry out tasks demanding significant responsibilities and involving stress, distraction, or crises, such as taking exams, driving a vehicle during heavy traffic, finishing a task within a time-limit or taking responsibility for a group of individuals.

d2400.title: Handling responsibilities
d2400.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions to manage the duties of task performance and to assess the requirements of these duties.

d2401.title: Handling stress
d2401.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions to cope with pressure, emergencies or stress associated with task performance, such as waiting for one's turn, taking deep breaths to remain calm, systematically looking for lost items and keeping track of time.

d2402.title: Handling crisis
d2402.description: Carrying out simple or complex and coordinated actions to cope with decisive turning points in a situation or times of acute danger or difficulty.

d310.title: Communicating with - receiving - spoken messages
d310.description: Comprehending literal and implied meanings of messages in spoken language, such as understanding that a statement asserts a fact or is an idiomatic expression.

d315.title: Communicating with - receiving - nonverbal messages
d315.description: Comprehending the literal and implied meanings of messages conveyed by gestures, symbols and drawings, such as realizing that a child is tired when she rubs her eyes or that a warning bell means that there is a fire.

d3150.title: Communicating with - receiving - body gestures
d3150.description: Comprehending the meaning conveyed by facial expressions, hand movements or signs, body postures, and other forms of body language.

d3151.title: Communicating with - receiving - general signs and symbols
d3151.description: Comprehending the meaning represented by public signs and symbols, such as traffic signs, warning symbols, musical or scientific notations, and icons.

d3152.title: Communicating with - receiving - drawings and photographs
d3152.description: Comprehending the meaning represented by drawings (e.g. line drawings, graphic designs, paintings, three-dimensional representations, pictograms), graphs, charts and photographs, such as understanding that an upward line on a height chart indicates that a child is growing.

d320.title: Communicating with - receiving - formal sign language messages
d320.description: Receiving and comprehending messages in formal sign language with literal and implied meaning.

d325.title: Communicating with - receiving - written messages
d325.description: Comprehending the literal and implied meanings of messages that are conveyed through written language (including Braille), such as following political events in the daily newspaper or understanding the intent of religious scripture.

d330.title: Speaking
d330.description: Producing words, phrases and longer passages in spoken messages with literal and implied meaning, such as expressing a fact or telling a story in oral language.

d335.title: Producing nonverbal messages
d335.description: Using gestures, symbols and drawings to convey messages, such as shaking one's head to indicate disagreement or drawing a picture or diagram to convey a fact or complex idea.

d3350.title: Producing body language
d3350.description: Conveying messages by intentional movements of the body, such as facial gestures (e.g. smiling, frowning, wincing), by arm and hand movements, and by postures (e.g. embracing to indicate affection or pointing to receive attention or an object).

d3351.title: Producing signs and symbols
d3351.description: Conveying meaning by using signs and symbols (e.g. icons, Bliss board, scientific symbols) and symbolic notation systems, such as using musical notation to convey a melody.

d3352.title: Producing drawings and photographs
d3352.description: Conveying meaning by drawing, painting, sketching, and making diagrams, pictures or photographs, such as drawing a map to give someone directions to a location.

d340.title: Producing messages in formal sign language
d340.description: Conveying, with formal sign language, literal and implied meaning.

d345.title: Writing messages
d345.description: Producing the literal and implied meanings of messages that are conveyed through written language, such as writing a letter to a friend.

d350.title: Conversation
d350.description: Starting, sustaining and ending an interchange of thoughts and ideas, carried out by means of spoken, written, signed or other forms of language, with one or more people one knows or who are strangers, in formal or casual settings.

d3500.title: Starting a conversation
d3500.description: Beginning an interchange, such as initiating turn-taking activity through eye-contact or other means, that leads to communication or dialogue, such as by introducing oneself, expressing customary greetings, or by introducing a topic or asking questions.

d3501.title: Sustaining a conversation
d3501.description: Continuing an interchange by taking turns in vocalising, speaking or signing, by adding ideas, introducing a new topic or retrieving a topic that has been previously mentioned.

d3502.title: Ending a conversation
d3502.description: Finishing a dialogue or interchange with customary termination statements or expressions and by bringing closure to the topic under discussion.

d3503.title: Conversing with one person
d3503.description: Initiating, maintaining, shaping and terminating a dialogue or interchange with one person, such as in pre-verbal or verbal play, vocal or verbal exchange between mother and child, or in discussing the weather with a friend.

d3504.title: Conversing with many people
d3504.description: Initiating, maintaining, shaping and terminating a dialogue or interchange with more than one individual, such as in starting and participating in a group interchange.

d355.title: Discussion
d355.description: Starting, sustaining and ending an examination of a matter, with arguments for or against, or debate carried out by means of spoken, written, sign or other forms of language, with one or more people one knows or who are strangers, in formal or casual settings.
inclusions: discussion with one person or many people

d3550.title: Discussion with one person
d3550.description: Initiating, maintaining, shaping or terminating an argument or debate with one person.

d3551.title: Discussion with many people
d3551.description: Initiating, maintaining, shaping or terminating an argument or debate with more than one individual.

d360.title: Using communication devices and techniques
d360.description: Using devices, techniques and other means for the purposes of communicating, such as calling a friend on the telephone.

d3600.title: Using telecommunication devices
d3600.description: Using telephones, computers and other electronic devices as a means of telecommunication.

d3601.title: Using writing machines
d3601.description: Using machines for writing, such as typewriters, computers and Braille writers, as a means of communication.

d3602.title: Using communication techniques
d3602.description: Performing actions and tasks involved in techniques for communicating, such as reading lips.

d410.title: Changing basic body position
d410.description: Getting into and out of a body position and moving from one location to another, such as getting up out of a chair to lie down on a bed, and getting into and out of positions of sitting, standing, kneeling or squatting.

d4100.title: Lying down
d4100.description: Getting into and out of a lying down position or changing body position, from horizontal to any other position, such as standing up or sitting down.

d4101.title: Squatting
d4101.description: Getting into and out of the seated or crouched posture on one's haunches with knees closely drawn up or sitting on one's heels, such as may be necessary in toilets that are at floor level, or changing body position from squatting to any other position, such as standing up.

d4102.title: Kneeling
d4102.description: Getting into and out of a position where the body is supported by the knees with legs bent, such as during prayers, or changing body position from kneeling to any other position, such as standing up.

d4103.title: Sitting
d4103.description: Getting into and out of a seated position and changing body position from sitting down to any other position, such as standing up or lying down.
inclusions: getting into a sitting position with bent legs or cross-legged
getting into a sitting position with feet supported or unsupported

d4104.title: Standing
d4104.description: Getting into and out of a standing position or changing body position from standing to any other position, such as lying down or sitting down.

d4105.title: Bending
d4105.description: Tilting the back downwards or to the side, at the torso, such as in bowing or reaching down for an object.

d4106.title: Shifting the body's centre of gravity
d4106.description: Adjusting or moving the weight of the body from one position to another while sitting, standing or lying, such as moving from one foot to another while standing.

d415.title: Maintaining body position
d415.description: Staying in the same body position as required, such as remaining seated or remaining standing for carrying out a task, in play, work or school.

d4150.title: Maintaining a lying position
d4150.description: Staying in a lying position for some time as required, such as remaining in a prone position in a bed.
inclusions: staying in a prone (face down or prostrate)

d4151.title: Maintaining a squatting position
d4151.description: Staying in a squatting position such as when sitting on the floor without a seat.

d4152.title: Maintaining a kneeling position
d4152.description: Staying in a kneeling position where the body is supported by the knees with legs bent for some time such as during prayers in church.

d4153.title: Maintaining a sitting position
d4153.description: Staying in a seated position, on a seat or the floor, for some time such as when sitting at a desk or table.
inclusions: staying in a sitting position with straight legs or cross-legged, with feet supported
staying in a sitting position with straight legs or cross-legged, with feet unsupported

d4154.title: Maintaining a standing position
d4154.description: Staying in a standing position for some time such as when standing in a queue.
inclusions: staying in a standing position on a slope
staying in a standing position on slippery surfaces
staying in a standing position or hard surfaces

d420.title: Transferring oneself
d420.description: Moving from one surface to another, such as sliding along a bench or moving from a bed to a chair, without changing body position.

d4200.title: Transferring oneself while sitting
d4200.description: Moving from a sitting position on one seat to another seat on the same or a different level, such as moving from a chair to a bed.
inclusions: moving from a chair to another seat, such as a toilet seat
moving from a wheelchair to a car seat

d4201.title: Transferring oneself while lying
d4201.description: Moving from one lying position to another on the same or a different level, such as moving from one bed to another.

d430.title: Lifting and carrying objects
d430.description: Raising up an object or taking something from one place to another, such as when lifting a cup or toy or carrying a box, or a child from one room to another.

d4300.title: Lifting
d4300.description: Raising up an object in order to move it from a lower to a higher level, such as when lifting a glass from the table.

d4301.title: Carrying in the hands
d4301.description: Taking or transporting an object from one place to another using the hands, such as when carrying a drinking glass or a suitcase.

d4302.title: Carrying in the arms
d4302.description: Taking or transporting an object from one place to another using the arms and hands, such as when carrying a pet or a child or other large object.

d4303.title: Carrying on shoulders, hip and back
d4303.description: Taking or transporting an object from one place to another using the shoulders, hip or back, or some combination of these, such as when carrying a large parcel or school-bag.

d4304.title: Carrying on the head
d4304.description: Taking or transporting an object from one place to another using the head, such when as carrying a container of water on the head.

d4305.title: Putting down objects
d4305.description: Using hands, arms or other parts of the body to place an object down on a surface or place, such as when lowering a container of water to the ground.

d435.title: Moving objects with lower extremities
d435.description: Performing coordinated actions aimed at moving an object by using the legs and feet, such as kicking a ball or pushing pedals on a bicycle.

d4350.title: Pushing with lower extremities
d4350.description: Using the legs and feet to exert a force on an object to move it away, such as pushing a chair away with a foot.

d4351.title: Kicking
d4351.description: Using the legs and feet to propel something away, such as kicking a ball.

d440.title: Fine hand use
d440.description: Performing the coordinated actions of handling objects, picking up, manipulating and releasing them using one's hand, fingers and thumb, such as required to lift coins off a table or turn a dial or knob.

d4400.title: Picking up
d4400.description: Lifting or taking up a small object with hands and fingers, such as when picking up a pencil.

d4401.title: Grasping
d4401.description: Using one or both hands to seize and hold something, such as when grasping a tool or a door knob.

d4402.title: Manipulating
d4402.description: Using fingers and hands to exert control over, direct or guide something, such as when handling coins or other small objects, such as scissors, shoe laces, pencils, chop sticks, knives and forks.

d4403.title: Releasing
d4403.description: Using fingers and hands to let go or set free something so that it falls or changes position, such as when dropping an item of clothing or a piece of food for a pet.

d445.title: Hand and arm use
d445.description: Performing the coordinated actions required to move objects or to manipulate them by using hands and arms, such as when turning door handles or throwing or catching an object.

d4450.title: Pulling
d4450.description: Using fingers, hands and arms to bring an object towards oneself, or to move it from place to place, such as when pulling on a string or pulling a door closed.

d4451.title: Pushing
d4451.description: Using fingers, hands and arms to move something from oneself, or to move it from place to place, such as when pushing a toy or an animal away.

d4452.title: Reaching
d4452.description: Using the hands and arms to extend outwards and touch and grasp something, such as when reaching across a table or desk for a book.

d4453.title: Turning or twisting the hands or arms
d4453.description: Using fingers, hands or arms to rotate, turn or bend an object, as is required to open a jar or use tools such as toothbrush or screwdriver.

d4454.title: Throwing
d4454.description: Using fingers, hands and arms to lift something and propel it with some force through the air, such as when tossing a ball.

d4455.title: Catching
d4455.description: Using fingers, hands and arms to grasp a moving object in order to bring it to a stop and hold it, such as when catching a ball.

d450.title: Walking
d450.description: Moving along a surface on foot, step by step, so that one foot is always on the ground, such as when strolling, sauntering, walking forwards, backwards, or sideways.

d4500.title: Walking short distances
d4500.description: Walking for less than a kilometre, such as walking around rooms or hallways, within a building or for short distances outside.

d4501.title: Walking long distances
d4501.description: Walking for more than a kilometre, such as across a village or town, between villages or across open areas.

d4502.title: Walking on different surfaces
d4502.description: Walking on sloping, uneven, or moving surfaces, such as on grass, gravel or ice and snow, or walking aboard a ship, train or other vehicle.

d4503.title: Walking around obstacles
d4503.description: Walking in ways required to avoid moving and immobile objects, people, animals, and vehicles, such as walking around a marketplace or shop, around or through traffic or other crowded areas.

d455.title: Moving around
d455.description: Moving the whole body from one place to another by means other than walking, such as climbing over a rock or running down a street, skipping, scampering, jumping, somersaulting or running around obstacles.

d4550.title: Crawling
d4550.description: Moving the whole body in a prone position from one place to another on hands, or hands and arms, and knees.

d4551.title: Climbing
d4551.description: Moving the whole body upwards or downwards, over surfaces or objects, such as climbing rocks, ladders or other objects.

d4552.title: Running
d4552.description: Moving with quick steps so that both feet may be simultaneously off the ground.

d4553.title: Jumping
d4553.description: Moving up off the ground by bending and extending the legs, such as jumping on one foot, hopping, skipping and jumping or diving into water.

d4554.title: Swimming
d4554.description: Propelling the whole body through water by means of limb and body movements without taking support from the ground underneath.

d460.title: Moving around in different locations
d460.description: Walking and moving around in various places and situations, such as walking between rooms in a house, within a building, or down the street of a town.

d4600.title: Moving around within the home
d4600.description: Walking and moving around in one's home, within a room, between rooms, and around the whole residence or living area.
inclusions: moving in a restricted area such as a courtyard, porch or garden

d4601.title: Moving around within buildings other than home
d4601.description: Walking and moving around within buildings other than one's residence, such as moving around other people's homes, other private buildings, community and public buildings and enclosed areas.
inclusions: moving inside, outside and around buildings, both public and private
moving throughout all parts of buildings and enclosed areas,
